text: Rare is the third studio album by American singer Selena Gomez, released by Interscope Records on January 10, 2020. As the executive producer, she collaborated with producers including Ian Kirkpatrick, Jason Evigan, Mattman & Robin, Sir Nolan, Simon Says, The Monsters & Strangerz, and David Pramik. Described by Gomez as her "diary from the past few years," the album is a midtempo pop and dance-pop record influenced by electronic, Latin pop, and R&B styles. Lyrically, it centers on themes of self-love, self-empowerment, self-acceptance, and self-worth. Guest features on the album include singer 6lack and rapper Kid Cudi. The album was promoted by two singles before its release: "Lose You to Love Me," released on October 23, 2019, topped the Billboard Hot 100 and became Gomez's first number-one single in the United States; "Look at Her Now," released the next day, peaked at number 27. The title track was released as the third single on the album's release day and reached number 30 on the Hot 100. Rare received positive critical reception, with many calling it Gomez's best album to date, and it earned a normalized Metacritic score of 76 based on 12 reviews, indicating generally favorable reviews. The album debuted at number one in Argentina, Australia, Belgium, Canada, Estonia, Lithuania, Mexico, Norway, Portugal, Scotland, and the United States, and was certified platinum by the RIAA for over 1 million equivalent units in the U.S. A Target-exclusive edition includes five standalone singles from 2017–2018: "Bad Liar," "Fetish" featuring Gucci Mane, "It Ain't Me" with Kygo, "Back to You," and "Wolves" with Marshmello. The vinyl edition adds "Feel Me" as a bonus track, and a deluxe edition with three new tracks, including the single "Boyfriend," was released on April 9, 2020. In a November 2019 interview for Apple Music, Gomez stated that the unreleased tracks were where she was at creatively and that the songs on the tracklist fit well together after being ordered. She also said on The Tonight Show Starring Jimmy Fallon that the album would have a "sense of strong pop" and that she experimented with electric guitar, adding that it took her four years to feel ready for the album. According to Semrush, Rare was one of 2020's three most-searched albums on Google, with 1.2 million monthly searches, alongside Taylor Swift's Folklore and J Balvin's Colores. The album is primarily pop and dance-pop with a dark tone, drawing from R&B, electro, funk-pop, reggaeton, alternative pop, and electronic music, with main themes of "love, loss and dating." Gomez described the album as "honest, empowering and uplifting," with core messages of self-love, acceptance, and empowerment, and stated that the songs are "the most honest music I've ever made." The standard edition contains 13 tracks, beginning with a quiet but impactful self-love anthem titled "Rare," which discusses a lover's wavering interest and the realization that the partner isn't valuing her adequately; its sound is described as muffled, as if "dunked underwater." The following track, "Dance Again," blends funk, dance, electro, and electropop, featuring an "infectious" and "mellifluous" melody, a "Cure-like" bass, "fuzzy" synths, and a "walloping disco bassline," and has been called "lite-Daft Punk" and "low-key yet deeply infectious." Co-written with Julia Michaels and Justin Tranter, "Look at Her Now" is an upbeat dance-pop and electropop track about moving on from a toxic relationship. "Lose You to Love Me," the only ballad, features "bare-bones" production with plucked violins, booming bass, tearjerker piano, an orchestra, and multi-tracked Gomez vocals, and is about self-love and discovering one's true self after losing a lover; critics speculated it may reference her relationship with Justin Bieber. "Ring," a Latin-infused track about toying with noncommittal lovers, draws comparisons to Camila Cabello's "Havana," Gotye's "Somebody That I Used to Know," and Santana's "Smooth." Produced by The Monsters & Strangerz with Jon Bellion, "Vulnerable" is a warm disco and electropop track with a moody synth groove and elements of italo disco and tropical house. "Let Me Get Me" features Latin music influences and is described as "dancefloor-ready." "Crowded Room," the first collaboration with 6lack, is an R&B song. Tracks 10, 11, and 12 have a funk sound; "Kinda Crazy" is a tongue-in-cheek, sinuous kiss-off driven by a clean bluesy guitar lick and horns; "Cut You Off" is a slinky, funk-inflected downtempo pop song about ending a draining relationship and has been compared to Taylor Swift. The album concludes with "A Sweeter Place," a collaboration with Kid Cudi that documents life lessons and expresses hope for brighter days. The vinyl and digital bonus editions include "Feel Me," previously on Gomez's 2016 Revival Tour setlist, released on digital platforms on February 21, 2020, the same day as the vinyl release. The album and its title were first announced on Gomez's Instagram page, which revealed the cover art and included a snippet of the title track. The standard edition was promoted by the release of "Lose You to Love Me" on October 23, 2019, and "Look at Her Now" on October 24, 2019; on November 24, 2019, Gomez performed both songs at the 2019 American Music Awards. She also promoted the album on The Tonight Show Starring Jimmy Fallon, The Ellen Degeneres Show, and The Kelly Clarkson Show. "Dance Again" was scheduled to promote CBS Sports and Turner Sports' 2020 NCAA tournament coverage but was not used due to the event's cancellation over the COVID-19 pandemic; proceeds from the song supported the MusiCares COVID-19 Relief Fund, and a performance video was posted on YouTube on March 26, 2020. In the U.S., Rare debuted at number one on the Billboard 200, earning 112,000 album-equivalent units (including 53,000 pure sales) in its first week, becoming Gomez's third U.S. number-one debut and the first album released in the 2020s to top the chart; it also accumulated 79.3 million on-demand streams that week. In its second week, it dropped to number six, earning 38,000 units; as of December 2020, it had 703,000 album-equivalent units in the U.S., and by July 2021, it had sold 123,000 pure copies. In the U.K., it debuted at number two, earning 17,661 album-equivalent units, becoming her highest-charting and highest-selling album in the country, and was certified gold by the BPI in April 2021 for 100,000 units. In Australia, it debuted at number one, becoming her first number-one debut there, and also achieved number one in Argentina, Belgium (Flanders), Lithuania, Portugal, and Scotland. Rare was featured on several year-end lists, including number 30 on Uproxx's "Best Albums of 2020," where editors noted its idiosyncratic lyrics, vocal performances, and earworm hooks; Rolling Stone ranked it number 24, with Julia Childing stating it was cathartic to hear Gomez release her past struggles, and also named "Cut You Off" the 19th best song of 2020; Billboard listed the title track as one of the best pop songs of 2020. UMI Yearlies named Rare album of the year in 2020.
